title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
author: Rob Lourens
description: Discover how we built the open Agent Host Protocol to keep your agent sessions accessible across editors, apps, phones, and the cloud. The post Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
summary: Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are.
takeaways: Each of these integrations solved the problem for one product, but developers also still want to be able to pull their agents into their own workflows–whether that’s an editor, a terminal, a phone, or a tool they built themselves–and they can’t do that if every client needs its own one-off integration.
The Copilot Chat extension, which used to provide all of VS Code’s AI and agentic capabilities, had been growing for over three years, reaching over 400,000 lines of TypeScript, not counting tests.
In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another.
